Known science foundations of Interstellar Probe Swarm Intelligence.

Swarm algorithms coordinate hundreds of robots on Earth. NASA's ANTS concept studied autonomous asteroid-belt swarms. Breakthrough Starshot proposes gram-scale laser-driven probes to Alpha Centauri. No interstellar probe has flown; Voyager 1, at 166 AU, takes 22 hours per one-way message.

Physical and engineering constraints on Interstellar Probe Swarm Intelligence.

Light-year delays force full autonomy; no real-time control is possible. Gram-scale probes have minimal power, sensing, and computation. Coordinating a swarm that cannot talk to Earth in real time is unsolved.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 16.2 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is Voyager distance vs Starshot probe mass at 16.2 orders of magnitude (Voyager distance larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
